title: Filler-Token Dependence Probe: Does the CoT Actually Compute Anything?

original_idea.body: Filler-Token Dependence Probe. Problem: no reusable diagnostic measures per task category how much accuracy survives when CoT is replaced with semantically empty filler of equal length. Direction: run each question with normal CoT, equal-length filler, and no CoT; measure accuracy drop; the gap is the load-bearing fraction; build a small benchmark reporting load-bearing fraction by task type.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: load-bearing fraction directly informs where CoT monitoring (a recognized critical pathway) can be trusted.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Clear inherited Lanham methodology; novice + mentor can execute on an open reasoning model.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused first deliverable; building a small benchmark adds modest scope.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Lab-independent CoT-monitoring work on open models.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only on an open reasoning model, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Filler-token test exists (Lanham); per-task turnkey tool may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Filler-token corruption is a known test; the systematized per-task diagnostic angle is plausibly open.
